name: Princeton Cocktail

instructions.primary_message: Combine gin (and simply syrup, if using) and bitters in a mixing glass and fill with ice. Stir well for 20 seconds and strain into a chilled cocktail glass. Gently pour the port down the inside of the cocktail glass, allowing it to slide down the side and settle in the bottom of the drink. Twist a piece of orange or lemon peel over the drink, but don't drop it in, as that will ruin the visual effect.

schema_metadata.keywords: alcohol, cocktails, drinks, gin, port, wine

description: The Princeton Cocktail dates to the late 19th century, when New York barman George Kappeler mixed them alongside other Ivy League-named drinks at the Holland House bar. Heavy and rich, a measure of port lends not only flavor to this drink, but an elegant appearance as it settles at the bottom of the cocktail glass.
notes: Optional substitutions: ruby port → tawny port
author: Paul Clarke
